Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From 642023d04335458a057b549da329ee4e30c8a838 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Sean Wang <sean.wang@mediatek.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2020 23:42:21 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] mt76: mt7615: fix up typo in Kconfig for MT7663U

Fix up typo in Kconfig with indicating MT7663U is an 802.11ac device

Fixes: eb99cc95c3b6 ("mt76: mt7615: introduce mt7663u support")
Signed-off-by: Sean Wang <sean.wang@mediatek.com>
Signed-off-by: Felix Fietkau <nbd@nbd.name>

diff --git a/drivers/net/wireless/mediatek/mt76/mt7615/Kconfig b/drivers/net/wireless/mediatek/mt76/mt7615/Kconfig
index e25db1135eda..c094260b0f89 100644
--- a/drivers/net/wireless/mediatek/mt76/mt7615/Kconfig
+++ b/drivers/net/wireless/mediatek/mt76/mt7615/Kconfig
@@ -35,6 +35,6 @@ config MT7663U
 	depends on MAC80211
 	depends on USB
 	help
-	  This adds support for MT7663U 802.11ax 2x2:2 wireless devices.
+	  This adds support for MT7663U 802.11ac 2x2:2 wireless devices.
 
 	  To compile this driver as a module, choose M here.
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/net/wireless/mediatek/mt76/mt7615/Kconfig`**
   - A typo was corrected in the help text for the `MT7663U` configuration. The description changed from:
     - "This adds support for MT7663U 802.11ax 2x2:2 wireless devices."
   - To:
     - "This adds support for MT7663U 802.11ac 2x2:2 wireless devices."

### Relationships
- The modification in the `Kconfig` file addresses a previously introduced bug related to the incorrect specification of the MT7663U device type. The fix clarifies that the MT7663U is an 802.11ac device rather than an 802.11ax device, which is crucial for accurate driver support and functionality. This change is linked to a prior commit (eb99cc95c3b6) that introduced support for the MT7663U, indicating that the typo was an oversight in that earlier implementation.

mt76: mt7615: fix up typo in Kconfig for MT7663U

Fix up typo in Kconfig with indicating MT7663U is an 802.11ac device

Fixes: eb99cc95c3b6 ("mt76: mt7615: introduce mt7663u support")
Signed-off-by: Sean Wang <sean.wang@mediatek.com>
Signed-off-by: Felix Fietkau <nbd@nbd.name>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by a typo in the Kconfig file where the MT7663U device was incorrectly labeled as an 802.11ax device instead of the correct 802.11ac. This misclassification could lead to confusion regarding the capabilities and compatibility of the device, potentially affecting driver compilation and functionality.
